Built with the required command (crt-static, --release --locked --offline --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the tree, nice -n 10 taskset -c 2,3); zero warnings; builds are reproducible (the same tree rebuilt byte-identically earlier: c2 == c3). Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock / Dockerfile byte-identical to rel16 (cmp verified). No comments in source, no new crates. Unit tests: cargo test 26 passed, 0 failed (log v5c/logs/cargo_test_c5.txt).\n- Intermediate binaries kept for the judge: bin/c2 (shape keys only, 59430690df62f605a03d5a9efef78fb55b58711377970968a325d21ce5b7c960), bin/c4 (+ bitmap dedup prefilter, 5acb480d15fa403c308d4e89606fb38abebb428183968c261b6bf0743deea560), bin/c5 (+ prefetch ring, final). bin/rel17 = 8400980a... (identical to rel17_work/bin/rel17).\n\nDESIGN (what the tree does now)\n1. src/fast/id.rs (new; replaces ident.rs). Every ID becomes a 16-byte Key {hi, lo} chosen by shape, never by inverting the generator bijection:\n   - short: domain prefix (0 or 1 byte, detected per column) + 1..11 lowercase base-36 chars -> hi = 0, lo = left-aligned base-36 rank over 11 positions (multiple of 36) + length. Lossless and canonical (string <-> (rank, len)); byte order of two shorts == numeric order of lo (rank order, length tiebreak). Leading zeros allowed (no need for the \"no leading zero\" rule; length is in the key).\n   - long: prefix + exactly 32 lowercase hex -> hi = first 16 hex digits, lo = last 16 (AVX2 nibble pack); hi in {0, 2^64-1} is sent to the fallback so classes never alias.\n   - odd: anything else (upper case, spaces, \\r, other lengths, other alphabets, other prefix, 31/33 hex, very long) -> hi = u64::MAX, lo = exact id from rel17's sharded exact intern table (kept only as the rare fallback: 1133 of ~26M keys on p20m5).\n   Equality of keys <=> byte equality of strings (the class is a function of the string, each class is injective). Byte-order comparison (person names, click-id ties): short/short by lo; long/long by (hi,lo); short/long by the 11-position rank against the long's first-12-hex-digit rank (prefix rule gives shorter-is-smaller); anything odd by materialised bytes. Tested exhaustively in id.rs (about 20k crafted + random strings x 4 domains: order, equality, round trip, lookup; also 400x400 full pairwise).\n   - Domain detection: the majority first byte over up to 4096 sampled lines of up to 64 files per column (users from events, else clicks, else links; event ids; click ids); no majority -> bare domain. Detection only affects speed, never correctness.\n2. scan.rs: rel17's mask scanner untouched; Kernel::mixed replaced by Kernel::short (16-byte shuffle/madd base-36, any length 1..11) and Kernel::long (32-byte hex decode); the SIMD-vs-scalar differential test extended (600k random buffers incl. quotes, NUL, 0xff).\n3. Records: Pair sinks with two lanes per stage: small lane with u64 keys when every key is short (EventSmall 32 B, PersonSmall 16 B, ClickSmall 24 B), wide lane with full Keys otherwise (EventRec 48 B, PersonRec 24 B, ClickRec 40 B). Sink staging generalised to multi-line stages (gcd-based) so 24/48-byte records still stream with non-temporal stores. On v5 data about 77% of copies take the small lane.\n4. Dedup (c4): per event partition a pair of bitmaps (seen-once / seen-twice, 2^10..2^18 slots, <= 64 KB, L1/L2 resident) over the event-key hash; copies in once-only slots are emitted directly (no table, no 48-byte conversion copy), only copies in twice slots (true duplicates + ~9% collisions) go to the exact index table (smallest ingest wins, invalid winners suppress copies, as before). Blocks recycled after the pass.\n5. People/union-find: slots are [Key; 2] (32 B), names picked with Domain::cmp; lookups (dedup winners, clicks) through a 64-entry prefetch ring (c5) instead of batch-32 prefetch-then-probe.\n6. Removed entirely: ident.rs (key recovery, lane F, mixed values, decoded person numbers, info/odd words, twist), choose_decoder, SESSIONS_LANE / SESSIONS_TEST_* knobs, LinkSets, lane-F statistics. Kept: rel17 scanner, unit scheduling (links/events/clicks queue, dedup queue, person partitions by size), arena + huge pages + populate + recycle, stale-file cleanup in output dirs, parquet writer, trace, and the general path (SESSIONS_PATH=slow) as fallback.\n   Not done (time): compact 16-byte copies (would need a right-aligned <=8-char key form plus partition remainders; estimated only ~0.1-0.2 CPU-s since copies are already 32 B), user-first routing with partition-local link resolution (report item 2, est. 0.3-0.6 CPU-s), binned sessionising (item 5, est. 0.2-0.4), parallel link parsing (links is a 0.2-0.35 s serial stage; on 8 scorer threads it is still shorter than the parallel events phase, so not on the critical path).\n\nMEASUREMENTS (p20m5 = 21.58M copies / 19.56M winners / 5.08M clicks, NCPU=2, nice 10, taskset 2,3; the box was shared with other engineers and Mech simulations, load 4-12 on 4 cores, so sys time varied 0.6-4.1 s between rounds of the same binary; paired medians are the reliable numbers)\n- rel17 vs c2 (3 interleaved rounds, v5c/logs/ab_rel17_c2.txt): CPU 12.87 -> 6.17 s median (min 5.21); paired -6.70 s, c2 lower 3/3 (user -5.59, sys -1.11).\n- c2 vs c4 (3 rounds): paired user -0.34 s (3/3), cpu -0.43 (2/3).\n- c4 vs c5 (3 rounds): paired cpu -0.04 (2/3), user -0.01 (3/3); cachegrind says c5 has +1.4% instructions (ring bookkeeping) for no measurable time change, so c4 and c5 are equivalent; c5 is the fully gated one.\n- rel17 vs c5 (5 rounds, v5c/logs/ab_rel17_c5.txt; one rel17 round was lost because I deleted stale run folders while it was writing, so n=4 for rel17): rel17 12.30 s (user 10.81, sys 1.63) vs c5 7.17 median / 5.14 min (user 5.21, sys 1.77);
